Per-source-document inventory. Each row points to a `<source-slug>.md` file that lists the section files derived from that source, with provenance metadata (commit, date, authors, ingestion date).

The rest of the endo corpus (~70 substantive markdown files: top-level, `docs/`, per-package READMEs, per-package `docs/` and `doc/` directories) is queued for future ingestion batches; the index will grow as those are filed.

| [symbol.js Hilbert-Hotel encoding for passable symbols](endo--packages-pass-style-src-symbol-js.md) | endojs/endo | packages/pass-style/src/symbol.js | 1-123 | The *passable-symbol surface* for @endo/pass-style. Defines what counts as a *passable symbol* (predicate + assertion), the bidirectional encoding between symbols and their wire-form string names, and an escape hatch for non-passable symbols. **Single most structurally interesting move**: the §Hilbert-Hotel encoding, *named explicitly in the file's JSDoc as a load-bearing trick*. The naive encoding `name → Symbol.for(name)` claims *every* string for registered symbols, leaving *no* room for well-known symbols. Hilbert-Hotel encoding shifts: `"@@iterator"` → `Symbol.iterator` (well-known); `"@@@@iterator"` → `Symbol.for("@@iterator")` (registered, shifted by one more `@@`); plain `"foo"` → `Symbol.for("foo")`. Two encoding spaces are disjoint because well-known names don't start with `@@` — asserted at module load as a host-platform invariant (§fail-at-load-not-at-use discipline). §Two-kinds-of-passable-symbols: registered (via `Symbol.for/keyFor`) + well-known (static symbol values on `Symbol` constructor); anonymous `Symbol(description)` excluded. §`wellKnownSymbolNames` Map built at module load via `ownKeys(Symbol)` + filter + identity-keyed-Map<symbol-value, `@@name`>. §Three-case-decoder `nameForPassableSymbol`: returns undefined for non-passable; double-prefix for registered-with-`@@`-prefix; `@@`-prefix for well-known; plain for registered. §Three-case-parser `passableSymbolForName` mirrors the encoder with the §forward-compatibility-via-throw discipline — *if name begins with `@@` it may encode a registered symbol from a future version of JavaScript, but it is not one we can decode yet, so throw*; §throw-rather-than-lose-identity rather than silently falling through to `Symbol.for` (the receiver might *later* gain the well-known symbol; silent fall-through would map pre-upgrade and post-upgrade messages to different symbols, breaking equality). §`AtAtPrefixPattern = /^@@(.*)$/` compiled and hardened at module load. §`unpassableSymbolForName(name) = Symbol(name)` — one-line escape hatch. §hideAndHardenFunction asymmetry: only on `assertPassableSymbol`. Foundational across the @endo/pass-style stack: cycle 71's passStyleOf dispatches `typeof === 'symbol'` here; cycle 69's encodeToSmallcaps and cycle 81's encodePassable both use `nameForPassableSymbol`; cycle 134's remotable.js's `@@toStringTag` allowance depends on this file's encoding. §Symbol-passability-as-pass-style-leaf observation. Key finding — an **asymmetry**: the fork realizes SES's *freeze* half (recursive C deep-freeze `JS_DeepFreeze`; two-phase freeze-all-intrinsics `JS_FreezeIntrinsics`; Compartment = fresh `JSContext` on the shared `JSRuntime`) but **omits the taming/permits half** (no permits whitelist, no intrinsic removal/repair, no determinism scrub, no `eval`/`Function`/`Error` taming; endowments cross as live parent-heap refs with no membrane). Verdict: **move the freeze into the engine** (safety-neutral speedup, no JIT) but **never drop the permits/taming** — a freeze-only `lockdown` is not a secure `lockdown`; and **reject** quickjs's shared-heap object passing in favor of XS's separate-heap marshaling membrane. ### Future-fork repositories (kriskowal's own repos, begin-ingest 2026-06-24)

These repos are kriskowal's own (forked under the bot account for future garden work) and given an initial faithful README ingest by the scholar on 2026-06-24. `kriskowal/frb` is now **fully ingested** (README plus the five grammar/compiler source files, cycle 4); `collections` and `cask` still have posted follow-on `scholar-ingest-<repo>` jobs for deeper material (per-package READMEs, the cask design docs and Go source). `kriskowal/gtor` (*A General Theory of Reactivity*) is now **fully ingested** (README in nine sections across three cycles, finishing 2026-06-24) — it is the conceptual root of the change-propagation cluster (FRB ↔ @endo/pubsub ↔ propagators). Distinct from the endo/agoric corpus: these introduce new cross-cutting topics (data-structures, reactive-bindings, change-propagation, content-addressed-storage, networking).

#### Collections per-package READMEs (begin 2026-06-24 via `scholar-ingest-collections`)

The per-structure idiomatic APIs. Each package's README sits at `packages/<name>/README.md` (last touched in the 2020-09-26 / 2020-11-06 monorepo reorg, file-commit `4688abad`). The first cycle (begin-ingest) ingested the four abstract mixins, the three notable operators, and the six core concrete structures (13 sources, 14 sections). The 2026-06-24 deepening cycle added the two `fast-*` indexes, the four LRU/LFU eviction families, `mini-map`, `iterator`, and the three `sorted-array*` structures (11 sources, 11 sections). The 2026-06-24 operator cycle (via `scholar-ingest-collections-operators`) added the eight generic operators (`clear`, `clone`, `has`, `hash`, `iterate`, `swap`, `to-array`, `zip`) and the `copy` micro-utility (9 sources, 9 sections), plus the [[polymorphic-operator]] concept page for their shared free-function-delegates-to-eponymous-method dispatch pattern. **The collections README corpus is now complete.** Note: `multi-map`, `sorted-map`, and `sorted-set` packages exist but ship **no README** at `4688abad`; the `operators` and `permute` packages likewise ship **no README** at `4688abad` (only `operators.js` / `permute.js`), so there is nothing to ingest for any of those.

### Gutentags component framework (Guten Tag; begin-ingest 2026-07-06)

Kris Kowal's **Guten Tag** ecosystem (`github.com/gutentags`): a reactive web-component framework that defines HTML tags as HTML/XML modules. `gutentags/gutentag` is the core package (loader plus the five building-block tags); the org also holds sibling *component packages* (`koerper` the virtual DOM, `wizdom` a minimal DOM subset, `system` the module loader, `blick` animation coordination, `kamera` focus management, `ndim` point/region types) and single-tag component packages (`list.html`, `dice.html`, `colorim.html`, `tengwar.html`, `accrete.html`). The first cycle (2026-07-06, `scholar-ingest-gutentag`) ingested the core `gutentag` README in full (14 sections), seeding the new [[html-modules]] topic. The second cycle (2026-07-06, `scholar-ingest-gutentag-packages`) ingested the three packages the gutentag README leans on directly — `koerper` and `wizdom` (new [[virtual-dom]] topic) and `system` (new [[module-loader]] topic) — plus `blick` (new [[animation-coordination]] topic). The third cycle (2026-07-06, `scholar-ingest-gutentag-remainder`) finished the sibling packages — `kamera` (new [[focus-management]] topic) and `ndim` (new [[spatial-geometry]] topic, design curated from source since the README is two lines) — and consolidated the four single-tag demo packages (`list.html`, `dice.html`, `colorim.html`, `accrete.html`) into one worked-example catalog section under [[html-modules]]. `tengwar.html` (no README) and `gutentag`'s own `essays/` example components (16 runnable components carrying only code — no README or design prose) were inspected and **skipped**; both would be re-ingested only if they grow documentation. The Guten Tag ecosystem ingest is complete.
